channel.title: Pier & Point · Mission Bay Kids' Park
channel.description: Changes, corrections and dated milestones for Mission Bay Kids' Park (Mission Bay), San Francisco. Every item names its source.

item.title: Correction · Mission Bay Kids' Park: An Urban Life Signs post dated June 30, 2016 announced the playground "will open July 1, 2016" (an announced date); Mission Bay Parks' post dated September 15, 2016 says the park is "finally open" with no day. SFist (May 26, 2016) says work "was finished months ago" and cites Board of Supervisors approval and unfinished streets; Urban Life Signs cites a land transfer.

item.title: Correction · Mission Bay Kids' Park: The Kids' Park summary gave the Long Bridge and China Basin location and the P6 label but cited only two articles that contain neither, and it called the opening day 'inconsistently reported'. It now also cites the SF Recreation and Parks facility page (the intersection) and OCII's open-space page (P6), and says that the Urban Life Signs blog gives July 1, 2016 while Mission Bay Parks' own post, dated September 15, 2016, gives no day. The 2015 milestone no longer mentions 'street work', which the blog does not say; it now says the fence stayed up pending a procedural land transfer to the city, with the area around it a construction site.

item.title: Complete · Mission Bay Kids' Park: Mission Bay Kids' Park playground opens to the public (~2016)
item.description: Mission Bay Kids' Park playground opens to the public (~2016). Source: Mission Bay Parks (missionbayparks.com), 2016-09; Urban Life Signs (community blog), 2016-06.
item.source: Mission Bay Parks (missionbayparks.com), 2016-09; Urban Life Signs (community blog), 2016-06

item.title: Under construction · Mission Bay Kids' Park: Playground construction visibly complete (grass grown in, play equipment and nature huts installed) but fenced off and not yet open to the public. Urban Life Signs (June 30, 2016) says it "appeared to be completed ... over a year ago" and attributes the closure to "transferring private redeveloped land over to the city"; SFist (May 26, 2016) says work "was finished months ago" and cites Board of Supervisors approval and, in the developer's statement, completion and acceptance of the streets fronting the park (Long Bridge and China Basin) (~2015)
